kinds.a: cold medicine · flu remedy · multi-symptom cold relief
kinds.d: Combination medicine for cold and flu symptoms, usually a painkiller with a decongestant and sometimes a cough or sedating ingredient.
t: day / non-drowsy — paracetamol (acetaminophen) with phenylephrine or pseudoephedrine
night — adds a sedating antihistamine such as promethazine, often with dextromethorphan
hot drink powder — paracetamol with phenylephrine, dissolved in hot water
capsule or tablet — the same combinations in solid form

kinds.a: oral antihistamine · hay-fever tablets · allergy tablets
kinds.d: Tablet, capsule or liquid antihistamine taken by mouth for hay fever and other allergy symptoms.
t: chlorphenamine (chlorpheniramine) — first-generation, drowsiness is a listed side effect
diphenhydramine or acrivastine — sold under Benadryl in some countries

kinds.a: hay-fever nasal spray · steroid nasal spray
kinds.d: Spray used in the nose for hay fever and other allergy symptoms.
t: steroid — fluticasone, mometasone, triamcinolone or beclometasone

kinds.d: Medicine that relieves a blocked nose, taken as a nasal spray or by mouth.
t: tablet or capsule — pseudoephedrine or phenylephrine

kinds.a: cough syrup · cough mixture · cough suppressant · expectorant
kinds.d: Syrup, liquid or tablet taken for a cough, either to suppress a dry cough or to loosen phlegm in a chesty cough.

kinds.a: throat lozenge · cough drop · cough sweet · pastille · throat spray
kinds.d: Medicated lozenge dissolved slowly in the mouth, or spray, for a sore throat or cough.
t: anaesthetic lozenge or spray — benzocaine, lidocaine or hexylresorcinol
anti-inflammatory lozenge or spray — flurbiprofen or benzydamine

brands.d: Reckitt's British brand of cold and flu remedies, best known for its lemon hot drink.
eras: Introduced as LEM-SIP 1969; renamed Lemsip in the 1970s

brands.d: Brand name from the Beecham Group, now used by Haleon in the UK for over-the-counter cold and flu products.
Kenvue brand of cough, cold and flu medicines; the flagship is marketed in some countries as Benylin DM.
Over-the-counter decongestant brand from McNeil (Johnson & Johnson), originally based on pseudoephedrine.
American over-the-counter brand owned by Procter & Gamble, maker of NyQuil, DayQuil, Formula 44, Sinex and VapoRub.
Reckitt brand of throat lozenges based on dichlorobenzyl alcohol and amylmetacresol.
American sore-throat spray and lozenge brand from Prestige Consumer Healthcare; the spray contains phenol.
British menthol cough-drop brand owned by Mondelēz International.
Cough-medicine brand made by Thornton & Ross of Huddersfield, part of Stada since 2013.
Kenvue antihistamine brand whose ingredients vary by country, including diphenhydramine, acrivastine or cetirizine.
Reckitt cough and cold brand built on guaifenesin products.
Haleon nasal decongestant brand based on xylometazoline (Otrivine in the UK).
Haleon multi-symptom cold and flu brand.
Haleon allergy nasal-spray brand based on fluticasone.
Haleon cough-medicine brand, including guaifenesin and dextromethorphan (DM) formulas.
Haleon night-time cold remedy containing paracetamol, promethazine and dextromethorphan.

notes: Shelf H2 Medicines & remedies / Cold, flu & allergy: there were 6 old kinds and there are now 6 kinds. Cough suppressant and Expectorant became one 'Cough medicine' kind with dry, chesty and combined (DM) types. 'Sore-throat lozenge & spray' is new; its source is the Wikipedia article Throat lozenge. Every type names its active ingredient(s), and there are no efficacy claims. Each kind lists 6–8 models covering UK, EU and US brands. Dropped: Rompe Pecho EX, a minor US product not needed to cover the market. Brand register: 16 entries, all from pages retrieved this session. Brands listed as model makers but not in the register: Zyrtec, Claritin, Allegra, Piriton, Piriteze, Xyzal, Flixonase, Nasacort, Nasonex, Beconase, Astepro, Afrin, Dristan, Delsym, Strepfen, Difflam, Tantum Verde. They have no register entry because I only retrieved ingredient pages that name them as trade names (the cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine, fluticasone, oxymetazoline, xylometazoline, azelastine, mometasone, triamcinolone, beclometasone, dextromethorphan and benzydamine articles), not pages about the brands themselves. Beechams range is listed as a range because I could not confirm current product names. I did not cover pholcodine cough products or Fisherman's Friend: the Fisherman's Friend fetch failed. The wiki and Wikidata tools failed (lock error, HTTP 429), so I used web_fetch for all sources. No traditions and no moves for this shelf.
